DISTRESS.description: High-pitched short bursts — possible meningitis or neurological irritability
DISTRESS.clinical_source: WHO Pocket Book: High-pitched cry = neurological distress flag
DISTRESS.action: EMERGENCY. Possible meningitis. Refer to facility immediately. Check fontanelle.

RESPIRATORY_DISTRESS.description: Weak breathy cry — respiratory distress at birth
RESPIRATORY_DISTRESS.clinical_source: WHO Essential Newborn Care 2024: Weak cry at birth = immediate assessment
RESPIRATORY_DISTRESS.action: EMERGENCY. Begin newborn resuscitation. Refer immediately.

PAIN.clinical_source: Neonatal cry research: Sustained high cry = pain or discomfort
PAIN.action: Assess for injury, infection, or feeding difficulty. Monitor closely.

HUNGER.description: Rhythmic repetitive cry — hunger or discomfort
HUNGER.clinical_source: Neonatal cry research: Rhythmic pattern = hunger or basic need
HUNGER.action: Feed the baby. Check nappy. Monitor for escalation.

NORMAL.clinical_source: WHO Essential Newborn Care: Vigorous cry within 30 seconds = healthy
NORMAL.action: No action required. Continue routine monitoring.
